description: 25 bounded editorial statement interpretations from already unresolved Stacks candidates; proof statements not accessed

decisions.expect_prefix: Let $f : Z \to X$ be a morphism
hypotheses: A morphism $f:Z\to X$ of locally ringed spaces; an open cover $X=\bigcup U_i$ such that each $f^{-1}(U_i)\to U_i$ is a closed immersion.
conclusions: The morphism $f$ is a closed immersion.

hypotheses: A module $M$ and a multiplicative subset $S$ of its base ring; a submodule $N'\subset S^{-1}M$.
conclusions: There exists a submodule $N\subset M$ such that $S^{-1}N=N'$.

hypotheses: The category of schemes.
conclusions: The category of schemes has a final object, products, and fibre products; equivalently, it has finite limits.

hypotheses: A finite Jacobson space.
A Jacobson space with finitely many closed points.
conclusions: The space is discrete.

hypotheses: A ring.
conclusions: Its prime spectrum is a spectral space.

decisions.expect_prefix: A scheme is an algebraic space
hypotheses: A scheme $T$.
conclusions: The representable functor $h_T$ is an algebraic space.

hypotheses: Two polynomials in $k[x]$ are relatively prime.
They have no common root in an algebraic closure of $k$.
conclusions: Two polynomials in $k[x]$ are relatively prime.
They have no common root in an algebraic closure of $k$.

hypotheses: The category of affine schemes and the category of rings.
conclusions: The first is equivalent to the opposite of the second, via global sections of the structure sheaf.

hypotheses: An arbitrary set.
conclusions: It belongs to $V_\alpha$ for some ordinal $\alpha$.

hypotheses: A ring $R$ and three $R$-modules $M,N,P$.
conclusions: $\Hom_R(M\otimes_R N,P)\cong\Hom_R(M,\Hom_R(N,P))$.

hypotheses: A finitely generated algebra over a Noetherian ring.
A localization of a Noetherian ring.
conclusions: The resulting ring is Noetherian.

hypotheses: A finite-type algebra over a field.
A finite-type algebra over $\mathbf{Z}$.
conclusions: The algebra is Noetherian.

hypotheses: A scheme.
conclusions: Its underlying topological space is locally quasi-compact.

hypotheses: An affine scheme.
A morphism from an affine scheme to a scheme.
conclusions: The scheme is separated.
The morphism is separated.

hypotheses: An abelian category $\mathcal{A}$.
conclusions: All finite limits and finite colimits exist in $\mathcal{A}$.

hypotheses: Two coverings of the same object $U$ in a site $\mathcal{C}$.
conclusions: There exists a covering refining both given coverings.

hypotheses: An equivalence relation $j:R\to U\times_S U$ over $S$.
conclusions: It extends uniquely to a groupoid $(U,R,s,t,c)$ over $S$.

decisions.expect_prefix: In a Karoubian additive monoidal category
hypotheses: A Karoubian additive monoidal category; a direct summand of an object with a left dual.
conclusions: That direct summand has a left dual.

hypotheses: A groupoid scheme $(U,R,s,t,c)$ over $S$.
conclusions: The morphism $j:R\to U\times_S U$ is a pre-equivalence relation.

hypotheses: A ring $R$ and the functor $C:\mathrm{Mod}_R\to\mathrm{Mod}_R$.
conclusions: The functor $C$ is exact and reflects injections and surjections.

hypotheses: An abelian variety.
conclusions: It is an abelian group scheme; its group law is commutative.

hypotheses: A morphism of sites $f:\mathcal{D}\to\mathcal{C}$ corresponding to $u:\mathcal{C}\to\mathcal{D}$.
conclusions: The associated adjoint functors $(f^{-1}=u_s,f_*=u^s)$ form a morphism of topoi.

hypotheses: An $M$-Koszul-regular sequence.
A Koszul-regular sequence.
conclusions: The respective sequence is $M$-$H_1$-regular.
The respective sequence is $H_1$-regular.

decisions.expect_prefix: The category $\Delta$ is the universal category
hypotheses: The simplex category $\Delta$ with objects $[n]$ and its face and degeneracy morphisms.
conclusions: It satisfies the stated universal generation and relations properties.

hypotheses: The property that a morphism is unramified.
The property that a morphism is G-unramified.
conclusions: Each property is fpqc-local on the base.
